To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we have proposed new measures to quantify the imbalance in MLC; 2) we have proposed two different approaches to deal with the imbalanced problem in MLC; and 3) we have shown that the imbalance in MCL is a problem that can be effectively solved using resampling techniques.

we have presented specialized measures directed to evaluate the imbalance in multilabeled datasets, and we have proposed four resampling algorithms that are able to reduce the imbalance level in a classifier independent way.

(1) the proposed imbalance measures are effective to assess the imbalance of a MLD and they are able to detect the imbalance in a MLD, and (2) the proposed resampling algorithms are effective to deal with imbalanced multilabel classification, and their performance is better than the performance of the state of the art methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of imbalance in multilabeled datasets and with the design of algorithms to deal with this problem.
the development of a set of tools that will allow to assess the imbalance in M LDs, and to reduce it in an appropriate way.
the development of new measures and algorithms to deal with the imbalance problem in the context of multilabel learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed measures are very useful to assess the imbalance of a given MLD, while the proposed algorithms are effective to reduce this imbalance, being the most appropriate one depending on the imbalance level and the number of labels in the problem.
the algorithms proposed in this work are useful to deal with the imbalance in multilabeled data, and they are able to improve the performance of any classifier.

the algorithms based on the label combination as class label are more appropriate for imbalanced MLDs, whereas the algorithms based on individual label imbalance levels should be applied when the imbalance is not so high, or when it is necessary to preserve the number of examples for each label.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed two different approaches to deal with imbalance in MLD.
, in the multilabeled scenario, it is not enough to consider the imbalance level of each label individually.
we propose a set of measures to evaluate the imbalance level of a given MLD, and four resampling algorithms to reduce the imbalance level in a MLD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to reduce imbalance in MLD, we must take into account the imbalance level for each label, as it is the main factor that affects the performance of the classifier.

the imbalance level in a MLD can be assessed by means of the proposed measures and that it is possible to reduce the imbalance of a MLD without knowing the classifier that will be employed in the future.
the imbalance in MlDs is an issue that must be taken into consideration in order to obtain a reliable classifier.
